raw_response:
I am 63 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for 25 years. I finished primary school. My farm is 16.1 mu, and I live alone. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone in this village. I have a well, so I pump water when I need it.

For wheat this year, I will do what I did last year because it worked. In October, I will hire a tractor with a rotary tiller to prepare the ground — 50 yuan per mu. I will buy improved wheat seed, about 30 jin per mu, which is 15 kg per mu. It costs me about 40 yuan per mu. I plant with a machine.

Before planting, I will spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. The bag is 100 jin, which is 50 kg. I use the 15-15-15 kind — the dealer told me once that means nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. That gives me some of all three. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with urea. I will spread 80 jin per mu, which is 40 kg. Urea is strong nitrogen. Altogether that is about 26 kg nitrogen per mu. I figured that out once with the dealer, but I mostly go by bags — two bags of fertilizer per mu for wheat is what I have always done, and last year my wheat was green and tall. I would rather put a little too much than too little. Two years ago, Old Wang tried to save money on fertilizer and his wheat was short and thin. He lost 300 jin per mu. I am not making that mistake.

I will irrigate four times from the well: once in winter, once at green-up in March, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Each irrigation costs me about 50 yuan per mu for diesel to run the pump.

For pests, I spray herbicide once in early spring to kill weeds. I spray insecticide twice — once for aphids, once if I see other bugs. I also spray fungicide once when the wheat heads. That is four pesticide sprays total.

I expect about 1000 jin per mu from the wheat, which is 500 kg per mu. Last year I got about that much.

For maize, after I harvest wheat in early June, I plant maize right away into the stubble without tilling. No-tillage saves me time and money, and the soil keeps moisture. I buy hybrid maize seed in packages — one and a half packages per mu, about 1.5 kg per mu. Costs about 60 yuan per mu.

At planting, I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows — that is 40 kg of 15-15-15. Then when the corn is knee-high, at the big trumpet stage, I spread 50 jin of urea per mu, which is 25 kg. That is about 17.5 kg nitrogen per mu, plus 6 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium from the compound. Hybrid corn needs a lot of nitrogen, everyone knows that.

I will irrigate twice: once when the corn is shooting up, and once at grain filling if it does not rain.

For pesticides, I spray herbicide once before the corn emerges, and insecticide twice for corn borer. That is three times total.

I expect about 1100 jin per mu from the maize, which is 550 kg per mu.

I have to watch my money because I am the only one in my household. But fertilizer is not where I cut costs. A bad harvest is a disaster. If I waste some fertilizer, that is just a few hundred yuan. If I lose yield, I lose thousands.
